items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Helvey also engaged Edgar Courance... and a trombone player... called Pluto... Once at a rehearsal, we were reading a number... the only one that kept going was Pluto

ctx.x: Page was not getting much work when I was offered a job to work in a Road House by a fellow named Wesley Helvey and as it was an every night affair I accepted to join him. I may have been lazy about doing other work but once I had gotten to the point where I could play something on my trumpet, I wanted to play as often as possible. I may have been late going to school at times or late getting to another kind of job, but I was never late when it came time to blow my horn.

Helvey also engaged Edgar Courance, who was now playing tenor sax, and a trombone player that had not been in Cincy very long. I don't remember his name except that he was called Pluto. There was a special water sold in drug stores at that time called Pluto water. Maybe this young fellow drank it and got the nickname in that manner. Pluto is also the name of the god of the underworld, but this fellow certainly was not the gangster type. One thing that he really could do was read music. Once at a rehearsal, we…

The pianist's name was Vincent Thomas and he was one of the few band pianists around town that could read music. The drummer was Leslie Towles and later a banjo player who's/only name I can remember was Jimmie, was added to the group.
